::: {#exm-constructive-proof}
#### Half of a positive number

Claim: for every positive real number $x$,
there is a positive real number $y$ with $y < x$.

Let $x$ be a positive real number.
We give a constructive proof of "there is a positive real number $y$ with $y < x$" for this $x$:
take $y = \frac{x}{2}$.
Then $y > 0$, because $x > 0$, and

$$
\ba
x - y
&= x - \frac{x}{2}
&& \text{(substitute } y = \tfrac{x}{2} \text{)}
\\&= \frac{x}{2}
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\\&> 0,
&& \text{(} x > 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

so $y < x$.
The element named, $\frac{x}{2}$, depends on $x$,
which a "for every $x$, there is a $y$" statement allows.

The solution to @exr-five-three is also a constructive proof:
it names the integers $2$ and $-3$.

:::
